question.text: Two rectangular blocks <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> of different metals have the same length and the same area of cross-section. They are kept with their lengths aligned and their cross-sections in contact. The temperature at one end of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and that of at the other end <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0 </mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. If the ratio of their thermal conductivity is <math><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, then under steady-state, what will be the temperature (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>) of the junction?

solution.text:
it is given that K1K2=13⇒K1=K  then K2=3K
The temperature of the junction in contact
θ=K1θ1+K2θ2K1+K2=1×100+3×01+3=1004=25 °C
